Shankarprasad Chowdhury.description: A businessman from Panihati and owner of the house Amaravati, whose family history and great-grandfather's possessions are central to the mystery.

Banwarilal Chowdhury.description: Banwarilal Chowdhury is Shankarprasad Chowdhury's great-grandfather, a barrister whose possessions are central to the mystery. He is sometimes referred to simply as Banwarilal.

Jayanta.description: Shankarprasad Chowdhury's cousin who is passionate about gardening and central to the events at Amaravati.

Ananta.description: The old servant who looks after Shankarprasad Chowdhury's aunt.

Naresh Kanjilal.description: Shankarprasad Chowdhury's business partner and one of the three guests present during the incident.

Dr Ardhendu Sarkar.description: A doctor from Panihati who treats Chowdhury's aunt and was present during the incident.

Kalinath Roy.description: An old school friend of Shankarprasad Chowdhury known for his sleight of hand and mysterious profession.

Panihati.description: A town by the Ganges river, where Shankarprasad Chowdhury's house, Amaravati, is located.

Ganges.description: A major river in India, considered sacred in Hinduism.

Amaravati.description: The name of Shankarprasad Chowdhury's ancestral house in Panihati.

Calcutta.description: A major city in India, now known as Kolkata.

Richard Leaky.description: An American scientist mentioned in relation to human evolution.

Lalmohan Babu.description: Lalmohan Babu, also known as Mr Ganguli and Jatayu, is Feluda's friend and a writer of thrillers who accompanies him on investigations.

Ambassador.description: A popular model of Indian car, used for the group's journey.

Salim Ali.description: A famous Indian ornithologist, author of 'Indian Birds'.

Ajoy Hom.description: Author of 'The Birds of Bengal', a book referenced for bird-watching.

Bhabatosh Sinha.description: The alias given to Mr Ganguli for their visit.

Gurkha.description: A member of a people from Nepal, often employed as guards in India.

Titagarh.description: A town near Panihati, where Shankarprasad Chowdhury works.

Rampur.description: A place where Banwarilal Chowdhury practiced as a barrister.

Nawabs.description: Muslim rulers or noblemen in India, historically significant.

Jehangir.description: A Mughal emperor of India, referenced in connection with the gold coins.

Ramayana.description: An ancient Indian epic, possibly the book seen with the aunt.

Mahabharata.description: Another ancient Indian epic, possibly the book seen with the aunt.

Namaskar.description: A respectful greeting in Bengali and Hindi, similar to 'hello'.

pyjama-kurta.description: A traditional Indian outfit consisting of loose trousers (pyjama) and a long shirt (kurta).

cheroot.description: A type of cigar with both ends clipped during manufacture, popular in India.

veranda.description: A roofed platform along the outside of a house, common in Indian architecture.

ghat.description: A series of steps leading down to a river, used for bathing or religious purposes.

paan.description: A preparation combining betel leaf with areca nut and sometimes tobacco, chewed for its stimulant effects.

bearer.description: A household servant or attendant, especially one who serves food or drink.

tika.description: A mark, often made with colored powder, applied to the forehead during Hindu rituals or celebrations.

prayer beads.description: A string of beads used to count prayers or mantras, common in Hindu and Buddhist traditions.

hand-grinder.description: A small, hand-operated device used to grind spices or other substances, common in Indian households.

rheumatism.description: A medical condition causing pain and inflammation in the joints or muscles, often referenced in India.

bridge.description: A card game popular in India, especially among the older generation.

Feluda.description: A famous private investigator known for his sharp observation and logical reasoning, who uses the alias Someshwar Roy and is also known as Mr Mitter.

hilsa.description: A popular and prized river fish in Bengali cuisine, often cooked with mustard.

Babu.description: A respectful Bengali honorific used for men, similar to 'Mr.'

Charminar.description: A brand of Indian cigarettes, popular and widely recognized.

Tapesh.description: Feluda's cousin and assistant who narrates the story, commonly known as Topshe and using the alias Prabeer.

Athenium Institution.description: An educational institution referenced as the workplace of Baikuntha Mallik, a poet.

Baikuntha Mallik.description: A poet and teacher at the Athenium Institution, admired by Lalmohan Babu.

hasnuhana.description: A fragrant night-blooming flower, also known as night jasmine or Cestrum nocturnum.

bed tea.description: Bed tea, also spelled bed-tea, refers to tea served in the morning, often brought to one's bedside as a customary practice in India.

sari.description: A traditional Indian garment worn by women, consisting of a long piece of cloth draped around the body.

alta.description: A red liquid dye traditionally applied to women's feet in India, especially during festivals or weddings.
